_comment: Which KAS pauseReason means a workflow step is waiting on a PERSON, as a table
both languages must satisfy.
The rule is implemented twice on purpose and neither copy can go, because they
answer different questions. The server's (internal/agent/run_ask.go
needInputPause) decides whether to reconstruct an answerable ask for a run this
process found already parked — the ask registry is in memory, so a container
restart leaves the run waiting with the question text gone. The client's
(static-src/run-store.ts isNeedInputPause) decides what a reader is told when
no ask reached this client at all, so the pause alert says a step is waiting for
an answer instead of restating a KAS literal.
This file is the contract between them, on internal/chat/testdata/
turn_outcomes.json's pattern. It is read by TestNeedInputPauseContract (Go) and
by run-store-pause.node.test.ts (TypeScript). A KAS wording change applied in
one language fails the other language's test, which is the only mechanism
keeping the two in agreement — there is no code generation for behaviour, and
the two failures it prevents are opposite and both silent: the server stops
reconstructing asks after a restart while the client keeps rewriting the alert,
or the reverse.
`reason` is the verbatim pauseReason string; `want` is whether it means a person
owes an answer. The three true spellings are KAS's own: send_message's park,
the fallback a plain Resume re-parks under (resume clears the run's pauseReason
and leaves the step node's completionSignal, so the next executeStep parks again
naming the node), and the same condition on a step that asked for a message.
The false rows are the OTHER pause reasons KAS writes, which must not reach the
predicate: mistaking one for a question offers a card nobody can answer, and it
would take the run's real reason off the reader's screen.

cases.name: send_message's own park
cases.reason: Step requested user input via send_message.

cases.name: the re-park fallback naming its node
cases.reason: Step 'review' is waiting for user input.

cases.name: the re-park fallback for a step awaiting a message
cases.reason: Step 'review' is waiting for the next user message.

cases.name: a node id carrying a quote does not break the match
cases.reason: Step 'it's here' is waiting for user input.

cases.name: an empty node id still matches
cases.reason: Step '' is waiting for user input.

cases.name: the restart-orphan reason is involuntary, not a question
cases.reason: Interrupted by agent restart; the previously running step was paused for resume.

cases.name: a transient network pause is involuntary
cases.reason: Transient connection error (EAI_AGAIN); the run is paused and can be resumed.

cases.name: an interrupted step is involuntary
cases.reason: Step interrupted (agent shutdown or connection reset); will resume.

cases.name: a near miss on the interpolated end is refused
a policy stop at maxIterations is not a question
a failed run is not a question
cases.reason: Run failed: the step exited non-zero.

cases.name: an empty reason is not a question
the prefix alone is not enough
the suffix alone is not enough
cases.reason: The build is waiting for user input.

cases.name: a near miss on the send_message literal is refused
cases.reason: Step requested user input via send_message
